fields.sections.4.exchanges.2.con.words: Bowen answers the protection reading by noting that Numbers 31 classifies the spared girls as plunder, undermining their portrayal solely as protected beneficiaries.
fields.sections.4.exchanges.2.con.critique: Strongest feature: Bowen answers the protective-beneficiary reading with the text’s own classification, observing that Numbers 31 places the spared girls among plunder and exposes tension in describing them as protected alone. Principal limitation: This responsive premise neither quotes the inventory nor explains its context, and classification as plunder does not itself establish the captives’ later status, treatment, or lack of protection. Live burden: Bowen must show why inclusion in the inventory defeats Knechtle’s account, while leaving Dillahunty’s separate property, consent, and autonomy conclusions to their actual speaker. Locked score: The fixed 82 rewards an auditable textual counterpoint that directly engages the preceding interpretation, while withholding greater credit because Bowen supplies only the classification and leaves its broader ownership and moral implications unstated.
